summary: postinstall dumps installer environment variables to /tmp/env
details: package.json declares a postinstall lifecycle script `env > /tmp/env` that fires automatically on `npm install`. The command bulk-writes every environment variable of the installing process to a fixed, world-observable path on the installer's host. On CI runners and developer machines the process environment typically contains credential-grade values (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, NPM_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, DATABASE_URL, and similar), so this constitutes credential harvesting at install time. The destination /tmp/env is readable by any local user on shared or multi-tenant hosts. The package name and version (`evilpostinstall`, `4192168.1.100` echoing an RFC1918 address) and the package's own stated description confirm the environment-capture is the intended behavior. No outbound network egress is present in the shipped files; the harm is local secret staging rather than direct exfiltration.
